ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), art. L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq.; Decree No. 2016-1618 of 28 Nov 2016 (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Act No. 2018-898 of 23 Oct 2018 (PACTE) sections on UBO declaration; EU AML Directives (EU) 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2018/1673; EU Regulation 2023/1113 on transfer of funds; TRACFIN reporting obligation under art. L.561-15.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each natural-person shareholder and of the proposed President (identity proof for the articles and the RBE file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority of the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Birth certificate (extrait d'acte d'état civil) of the proposed President (required where the articles are executed before a notaire or where a bank demands notarised incorporation documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry of the jurisdiction of birth

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing or recent registry excerpt for any corporate shareholder holding 25% or more of the SAS share capital (required to pierce the UBO chain through the corporate layer)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney in favor of the filing attorney and local representative (mandat sous seing privé), with legalized signature where the incorporation is effected remotely
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary or French consular officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory systematic screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories before filing: (i) automated watch-list check against the EU consolidated sanctions list (Regulations 269/2014 and 833/2014), the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list and French DG Trésor asset-freezing decisions under art. L.562-1 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code; (ii) PEP determination under the FATF definition of prominent public function, applied consistently with ACPR/AMF/TRACFIN guidance; (iii) enhanced due diligence (EDD) immediately triggered if any PEP, high-risk third country or listed entity is identified, including an obligation to file a suspicious-transaction report with TRACFIN; (iv) for this Low_Risk_Standard vertical CRM/ERP software entity with no regulated activity, French law permits simplified due diligence (SDD) on the commercial counterparty, but the RBE declaration and UBO verification remain unconditional requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with pre-clearance searches performed via INPI Data (data.inpi.fr), the EUIPO trademark database and Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr); RCS registration is effectuated through the competent Greffe du Tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin characters; the official RCS register records the name in French. Where the chosen identifier originates in a non-Latin script (Chinese, Cyrillic, etc.), a sworn French transliteration and translation are mandatory and the transliterated form becomes the registered denomination. The name must be lawful, distinctive and not misleading, and must not infringe a prior French trademark (art. L.711-4 of the Intellectual Property Code) or an existing French company name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (where it implies official public character)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a separate statutory pre-incorporation name reservation; the name is validated and registered through the articles of association and the RCS filing. Upon a post-filing rejection: (1) request the Greffe's written reason (motivation) within 8 days; (2) submit a corrective filing by modifying the denomination or by obtaining a withdrawal/opposition settlement with the prior trademark or name holder; (3) if the conflict is not resolved, challenge the refusal before the President of the Tribunal de commerce for the registered seat, or bring an unfair competition action under art. 1240 of the French Civil Code against the prior rights holder; (4) alternatively, re-file with a permissible distinctive element and preserve the commercial priority date. No ministerial appeal lies to INPI in respect of company-name refusals; the remedy is judicial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry subject to art. L.123-11-2 and R.123-121 of the French Commercial Code. The SAS may domicile its registered office at a licensed domiciliation company or at the President's residence for an initial period not exceeding five years. For a pure vertical-cloud software vendor without physical premises, domiciliation with an authorized business center is acceptable and does not by itself create a French permanent establishment for corporate income tax purposes. The registered office must remain genuinely accessible for service of process, and the public registry file must contain no inconsistent address. Economic substance is adequate where the SAS maintains a President, a French/European bank account, accounting records, and declared VAT/corporate income tax arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annually for a standard ICT entity with no regulated license. The likelihood rises to 10–15% where VAT, transfer pricing or substance indicators deviate from the declared activity, or where the company reports consecutive losses during the tax audit assessment window (art. L.13 of the LPF). Unannounced premises visits (visite domiciliaire) under art. L.16B of the LPF require judicial authorization and are exceptional for non-suspicious software companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), L.210-1 to L.210-12 (Company Formation), and regulatory provisions R.227-1 et seq.; also Order of 26 June 2025 on the national one-stop company formalities platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), filing made via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises managed by INPI in partnership with Infogreffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified Statuts (articles of association) forming the SAS, together with the beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) and the deed of appointment of corporate officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SAS has no statutory minimum capital; capital is freely fixed by the shareholders. The capital must be fully subscribed before registration. Cash contributions may be paid up within five years, provided that at least one-half of each cash contribution is deposited upon subscription/formation, and in-kind contributions must be fully transferred at the moment of subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders accept and subscribe in full to the share capital of 1,000 EUR divided into 1,000 ordinary shares, and the chairman is authorized to effect all cash contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office is hereby established at [registered address], and this place of administration shall be recorded in the articles of association. RESOLVED, that the appointment of [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chairman is ratified, with powers extended by applicable French commercial law. RESOLVED, that the officers are fully authorized to complete the registration dossier with the competent Commercial Court Registry, to appoint any nominee representative, and to satisfy all publication and filing formalities. RESOLVED, that this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and sign the articles of association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and optionally a notaire; the final statutes must be filed through the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statutes in French specifying corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose (ISIC 6201 software development and cloud services), share capital, share classes, duration, chairman, chief executive officer powers, decision-making rules, and transfer restrictions. Execute the document by all shareholders. If contributions in kind are made, appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux apports) to produce a valuation report unless unanimous shareholder consent waives it.
required_dossiers: Signed statutes (exemplaire original séparé and deposit copies)
In-kind contribution valuation report or shareholder consent waiver
Letters of acceptance of office by the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
Copy of identity documents of all shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the statutes for legal deficiency, amend the clauses to meet French Commercial Code requirements and re-execute the corrected version before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a legal notice of incorporation (Avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement gazette (Journal d'annonces légales) approved by the relevant Commercial Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the incorporation notice to an approved legal announcement journal for the department where the registered office is located. The notice must state the corporate form, exact company name, capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, officers, and the registry where registration will occur. Obtain the attestation de parution upon publication.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation announcement in French
Proof of payment of publication fee
Requested date of publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal is not an approved legal announcements periodical or the notice is inaccurate, republish the corrected announcement in an admissible journal and obtain a new attestation de parution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the mandatory beneficial ownership section in the one-stop filing portal, identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds or controls more than 25% of the SAS' capital or voting power, or who otherwise exercises control of the company. Attach a separate declaration and executive identity documents as required by the French Code monétaire et financier.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owner declaration form
Passport or copy of national identity card of each disclosed beneficial owner
Organizational chart or ownership documentation demonstrating the chain of control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the control structure is unclear or shell-ownership indicators are detected, amend the declaration with the precise chain of control and supporting legal instruments before the registry issues a formal rectification request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the full incorporation dossier and pay registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique (INPI / infogreffe portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official one-stop business formalities platform, select the French SAS application path, and upload all statutory documents. Verify data consistency between the statutes, beneficial owner declaration, publication notice, and officer appointments. Electronically pay the registry fee and related state taxes. Submit the dossier for legal formality control.
required_dossiers: Final signed statutes
Attestation de parution from the legal announcements journal
Beneficial owner declaration with supporting identities
Proof of registered office authority (lease agreement, co-working certificate, or property ownership title)
Officer acceptance letters and valid identity documents
Bank capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) for cash contributions
Payment confirmation of the filing fee and publication tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is formally queried, the registry will issue an injunction to regularize (injonction de régularisation). The applicant has 30 days to cure the defect by supplementary filing, amended documents, or explanation; failure to cure leads to closure of the application without admission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive RCS registration and generate post-formation identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the registry approves the dossier, obtain the Kbis extract, SIREN number, SIRET establishment number, and French business registration certificate. Ensure the legal entity is now operational for corporate governance purposes and proceed with necessary declarations to the tax, social, statistical, and data protection authorities.
required_dossiers: Registry decision approving the formation
Kbis extract and company identifiers (SIREN, SIRET, NAF code of 6201Z)
Registered address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis extract is delayed or shows erroneous data, submit a written rectification request to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce with supporting statutes and proof of deposit; request an expedited correction of the SIREN/SIRET record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Collect final capital release documentation and activate corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France and the SAS management body
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the bank account is opened in the SAS name with funds blocked under attestation de dépôt des fonds. After registration, release the deposit to the company treasury in accordance with the statutes. Update the registered office and banking signatures, and issue definitive share certificates to all shareholders.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account opening agreement
Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds
Kbis extract as proof of legal existence
Registered office lease or proof of office occupancy
Mailbox invitation letter (if required by the bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank resists releasing the blocked funds without a Kbis extract, provide the final Kbis and a board resolution expressly certifying the company's RCS number and registered office; if the bank unreasonably delays, engage the Banking Mediator (Médiateur du crédit).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) – no industrial license is required for cloud/software activities under NAF 6201Z
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; the activity is classified as low-risk administrative software services and is exempt from ICPE industrial authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion / DREAL (Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA Report or registration is required for a pure software/cloud CRM business with no physical production plant, extraction activity, or material effluent discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial wastewater or volatile organic compounds (VOCs); if the SAS later operates its own data centers or significant server rooms, it will need to comply with EU Energy Efficiency Directive standards (CEmA / EN 50600), RFI/electrical hazard rules, and waste electrical and electronic equipment (DEEE) recycling obligations. No industrial discharge thresholds apply to standard office environments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to industrial infrastructure. If physical offices are occupied, the SAS must comply with the French Labour Code (Code du travail) on workplace health and safety, ergonomic workstation standards, fire safety compatibility of the premises, and, where applicable, local accessibility regulations. No civil defense structural clearance is required for a pure vertical SaaS/CRM enterprise.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP); online portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional space); SIRENE/INSEE for SIREN/SIRET issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first register with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) via a French commercial court to obtain a SIREN (9-digit legal entity identifier) and SIRET (14-digit establishment identifier). For non-resident entities without a French establishment but liable for VAT, registration is made directly with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) using form Cerfa 11908 (VAT registration) and supporting documents: certificate of incorporation, proof of legal representative identity, and a power of attorney if an agent is used. Upon validation, a French VAT number (FR + 2 check digits + SIREN) is issued. The process is typically completed within 2–4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box regime. Specific elections include: (i) option for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for groups with ≥95% ownership; (ii) option for the parent-subsidiary regime (régime des sociétés mères et filiales) under Articles 145 and 216 CGI allowing 95% dividend exemption; (iii) election to be taxed as a partnership (société de personnes) is not available for SAS; (iv) possible to opt for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C CGI for closely linked entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for foreign entities making taxable supplies in France. For domestic small businesses, simplified VAT regime thresholds: 85,000 EUR for goods and 37,500 EUR for services under the franchise en base scheme; however, non-resident entities with a fixed establishment or making distance sales above 10,000 EUR to French consumers must register immediately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing (Facturation électronique) progressively: from July 2024, all companies must accept e-invoices; from July 2025, large and mid-sized companies must issue e-invoices; from January 2026, all companies must issue e-invoices. The system requires transmission through a Chorus Pro portal or an approved platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire, PDP) with real-time clearance and digital stamping. Non-compliance penalties: 15 EUR per invoice, capped at 15,000 EUR per calendar year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 262 I CGI. Services supplied to non-EU customers are zero-rated under Article 259 A CGI if the customer is established outside the EU and the service is not related to immovable property in France. For B2B services, the place of supply is the customer's location, so no French VAT applies (reverse charge).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation, DAU) lodged with French customs (Douane)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving payment
Commercial invoice with VAT number and export mention
Proof of exit of goods from EU territory (certified by customs)
Contract or purchase order for services
Proof of customer's non-EU establishment (e.g., VAT number, certificate of incorporation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax authorities (DGFiP) conduct rigorous audits for export zero-rating. Penalties for fraudulent claims include: retrospective assessment of the evaded VAT plus a 40% surcharge for deliberate breach (Article 1729 CGI), 80% in cases of fraudulent intent, and criminal penalties under Article 1741 CGI (up to 5 years imprisonment and 500,000 EUR fine). Additional penalties for failure to provide documentation: 50 EUR per missing document. Clawback period: 3 years (normal) or 10 years for fraudulent activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-exchange and payment-services supervision is supplemented by the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution), the French Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor), and customs authorities where trade reporting is relevant.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and generally applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under European Union law. There are no general French foreign-exchange controls, capital repatriation restrictions, mandatory resident foreign-currency surrender rules, or routine central-bank approval requirements for inbound equity, shareholder loans, dividends, royalties, service fees, or other lawful cross-border payments. Transactions remain subject to bank customer due diligence, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rules, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner verification, tax documentation, transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, and possible reporting obligations. Dividend distributions by a Société par Actions Simplifiée require distributable profits, approved financial statements, applicable statutory-reserve compliance, and corporate approvals. Payments to related non-residents must be commercially supported and arm's-length. French withholding tax, treaty relief, European Union exemptions, and anti-abuse rules must be assessed before remittance. Banks may delay or reject transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions, opaque ownership, unexplained source of funds, unusual payment chains, or insufficient commercial evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a French bank, convert export receipts into euros, or convert them within a prescribed period. Export proceeds may generally be retained in euro or foreign-currency accounts, including accounts outside France, subject to accurate accounting, tax reporting, customs and trade documentation, sanctions compliance, and bank-specific transaction monitoring. Payments received through SEPA, SWIFT, card-acquiring, or other regulated channels must be reconcilable to invoices and contracts. Cash transactions and cross-border cash movements remain subject to European Union and French declaration and anti-money-laundering rules. Export-control, customs, VAT, and Intrastat obligations may apply independently of foreign-exchange rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
Banque Populaire Rives de Paris, a Banque Populaire network institution of Groupe BPCE
Caisse d'Épargne et de Prévoyance Île-de-France, a Caisse d'Épargne network institution of Groupe BPCE

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, SEPA payment initiation, direct-debit processing, card acquiring, and treasury sub-accounts, provided the provider is authorized under the Payment Services Directive or Electronic Money Directive and is passported or otherwise lawfully operating in France. An offshore digital EMI without French or European Economic Area authorization, passporting, or an authorized local partner cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to the French SAS. An EMI is not a credit institution and generally cannot accept repayable deposits or provide a conventional bank overdraft. Customer funds must be safeguarded rather than treated as bank deposits. The company should verify authorization in the European Banking Authority or relevant national register, safeguarding structure, SEPA reachability, French customer-service capability, sanctions controls, data-processing arrangements, insolvency protection, account-closure rights, and access to cash-management APIs. A regulated EMI account should not be the sole account for payroll, tax, capital funding, or critical liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal French statutory requirement for all directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, certified corporate documents, video identification, electronic signatures, and enhanced verification. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, a local authorized signatory, a French address, a video interview, original or apostilled documents, or verification of the ultimate beneficial owner. Capital escrow procedures for incorporation are bank-specific and may require wet-ink or certified documents. Directors, authorized signatories, shareholders holding controlling interests, and beneficial owners should be prepared for individual identity verification and source-of-wealth questioning.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent, shareholder, director, or beneficial owner with an ownership chain involving multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extracts for every intermediate entity; constitutional documents; certified ownership chart through the natural-person beneficial owners; passports and address evidence for relevant individuals; board or shareholder resolutions; tax-residency information; and a concise explanation of the group structure and commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, bearer-style interests, trusts, foundations, or discrepancies between corporate records and onboarding declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed beneficial-owner declaration; registers of shareholders and directors; trust or foundation instruments where applicable; independent corporate search reports; notarized or certified translations; and a reconciliation memorandum explaining all voting, economic, and control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital or shareholder-loan funding from an account that is not held in the name of the shareholder or that passes through an unexplained third-party account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement or loan agreement; shareholder bank statements; proof of source of funds and source of wealth; payment-chain explanation; board approval; tax and accounting treatment; and a written instruction that funds be remitted directly from the disclosed funding party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model described as software or cloud services but showing payment flows resembling money transmission, marketplace settlement, stored value, crypto activity, or regulated financial services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business-process map; customer and supplier contracts; terms of service; product screenshots; data-flow and funds-flow diagrams; confirmation that the SAS does not hold customer funds or provide regulated payment services; relevant legal analysis; and any required registration or licensed-partner agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume international receipts, rapid movement of funds, substantial transactions with unrelated jurisdictions, or payment descriptions inconsistent with the ERP and CRM software business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier master files; signed invoices and contracts; delivery or acceptance evidence; transaction-level reconciliation; expected-country and expected-currency matrix; pricing policy; and management explanation of seasonality and payment cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, high-risk, embargoed, or heavily monitored jurisdictions, counterparties, banks, or beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy; documented screening results; counterparty ownership checks; end-use and end-user statements; export-control classification; licenses or government authorizations where applicable; and evidence that prohibited transactions are blocked.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person status, criminal allegations, litigation, insolvency, or regulatory enforcement involving a director, shareholder, beneficial owner, customer, or major supplier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal and compliance memorandum; official court or registry records; explanation of the event; disposition documents; enhanced due-diligence report; certified identity documents; and board-approved risk-mitigation measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recently incorporated SAS with no operating history, no French employees, no local office, or projected turnover materially exceeding demonstrated operational capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; signed customer pipeline; employment and outsourcing agreements; office or registered-address evidence; technology and hosting contracts; founder biographies; capitalization table; 12-to-24-month financial model; and evidence of initial operating expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-risk indicators, including unexplained related-party payments, royalty flows, unusually low French margins, or inconsistent VAT and corporate-tax information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; benchmarking where appropriate; invoice samples; VAT registrations and filings; tax-residency certificates; withholding-tax analysis; group organization chart; and confirmation of accounting controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual offices, mail-forwarding addresses, personal accounts, personal payment cards, or shared banking credentials for company operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or valid registered-office documentation; proof of operating location; dedicated corporate account policy; signatory matrix; board resolution; expense policy; and evidence that company funds are segregated from personal funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete, expired, untranslated, unauthenticated, or internally inconsistent corporate documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; current articles of association; certified translations where requested; apostilles or legalization where required; notarized copies; updated powers of attorney; and a document index showing issue dates and validity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in share capital to the French SAS capital-deposit account from the subscribing shareholder's account in the shareholder's legal name, using a bank subject to applicable AML controls. Provide the draft or executed articles of association, subscription statement, shareholder resolution, capitalization table, corporate-registration evidence, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and the bank's requested transfer narrative. After incorporation, transfer operating liquidity to the SAS operational account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-euro payments. Use an accurate purpose description such as 'paid-in share capital', 'shareholder loan under agreement', or 'intercompany funding under agreement'; do not use generic or misleading descriptions. Retain MT103 or equivalent payment confirmation, creditor and debtor details, intermediary-bank data, invoice or agreement references, and accounting entries. Reconcile each receipt to the shareholder ledger and report it consistently in the French accounts. Shareholder loans require written terms, arm's-length interest analysis where relevant, corporate approvals, and tax and transfer-pricing review. France does not generally require prior central-bank approval for these injections, but the receiving bank may request enhanced verification before crediting funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro supplier, payroll, tax, and intra-European payments where available. Use SWIFT MT103 or the applicable ISO 20022 cross-border payment message for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments, with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, bank, purpose, invoice, and sanctions-screening information. Use documentary Commercial Letters of Credit, including irrevocable documentary credits, where supplier, jurisdiction, goods, or counterparty risk justifies bank-controlled document presentation. For software and cloud services, ordinary bank transfers, card acquiring, SEPA Direct Debit, and contractual subscription billing are generally more suitable than documentary credits unless physical goods or material implementation deliverables are involved. Maintain invoices, contracts, acceptance records, tax documentation, customs records where applicable, beneficiary verification, and payment approvals. Treasury should apply dual authorization, segregation of duties, payment limits, callback verification for changes in beneficiary details, daily bank reconciliation, and sanctions screening. Do not route funds through personal accounts, unregulated money transmitters, or undisclosed third parties. Intercompany service fees, royalties, and reimbursements require written agreements, transfer-pricing support, VAT analysis, withholding-tax review, and evidence of services received.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized credit institution or regulated investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed commercial exposures and supported by a treasury policy, exposure register, maturity matching, counterparty limits, and confirmation controls.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited delivery markets, subject to the counterparty's regulatory permissions, applicable market-abuse and sanctions rules, EMIR obligations, collateral and reporting requirements, and documented underlying exposure. NDFs should not be used for speculative activity without appropriate governance.

Foreign-currency swaps and cross-currency swaps with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm for funding or liquidity management, supported by documented cash-flow requirements, valuation controls, collateral terms, close-out provisions, and accounting treatment.

Foreign-currency options and option collars where commercially justified and approved under the treasury policy, with clear assessment of premium, leverage, maximum loss, suitability, and accounting consequences.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and payments, currency bank accounts, intercompany netting, and contractual currency clauses, subject to proper documentation and transfer-pricing and accounting treatment.

All derivative activity should comply with applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation requirements, including trade reporting, risk-mitigation, clearing or collateral obligations where applicable, and counterparty documentation such as an ISDA Master Agreement and collateral annex when appropriate. The SAS should avoid leveraged or opaque products that are disproportionate to its operating exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the sole shareholder (SAS decision) with president's management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record - minutes recorded in the Registre des décisions de l'associé unique; auditable by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year end); court-ordered extension possible on petition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prevents the legal deposit of accounts; court injunction with astreinte; personal liability of the president; persistent failure supports administrative strike-off of RCS registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual filing of financial statements: balance sheet, profit and loss, annexes, management report) with publication option - official RCS tariff EUR 46 (approx. USD 50)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce on the RCS - guichet-entreprises / e-procédures portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval (2 months for paper filing); calendar-year SAS practical deadline 31 July; court extension up to 6 months possible (C. com. art. L.232-23)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: commercial court injunction with astreinte, late penalty, inability to certify compliance; repeated default leads to RCS administrative strike-off and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation/update of beneficial owners declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs - DBE) with the annual accounts deposit - official tariff EUR 22 (approx. USD 24)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS; accessible to TRACFIN and competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On incorporation and within 30 days of any change; annual re-confirmation integrated with the closing accounts deposit (no-change validation accepted if data still accurate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 7,500 (individuals) and EUR 37,500 (legal entities); the registry may refuse other RCS filings; reputational and AML screening risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return - Déclaration de résultats No. 2065-SD with full liasse fiscale (IS return and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (electronic EDI-TDFC filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Off-calendar year end: within 3 months of the fiscal year close; for a 31 December year end: second working day after 1 May (FY 2024 return due 5 May 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 10% of the tax due (40% after formal notice, 80% for fraudulent intent); monthly late interest of 0.20%; triggers tax assessment and audit exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration et paiement de la Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) - annual local business property contribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) of the establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration by 15 May of the assessment year (activity existing on 1 January); payment by 15 December of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty plus 0.20% monthly interest; privileged tax lien on business assets; provisional assessment if declaration omitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit - verification of the Register of Securities Movements, decisions/minutes register and secretary books before the annual approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; internal governance record to present to the statutory auditor, RCS registrar on control, and tax auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each year before the shareholder approval; register of securities movements must record every transfer in real time during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective registers can invalidate share-transfer evidence and minutes, generate director liability and prevent clean accounts filing and capital operations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For fiscal years starting on or after 1 January 2024, mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) where the SAS exceeds two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 5.0M, net turnover (ex-VAT) EUR 10.0M, average permanent staff of 50; audit also compulsory for controlled/controlling group situations or on the request of shareholders holding at least one-third of the share capital (C. com. L.823-1, L.823-3; Decree 2023-1142)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP - Plan Comptable Général (PCG) per C. com. L.123-12 to L.123-28; IFRS as endorsed by the EU solely for consolidated accounts of listed groups in scope

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial-owner declaration (DBE) filed at RCS at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in direct/indirect ownership over 25% or voting control; the annual accounts deposit is the annual re-confirmation point - registry cross-checks the DBE; if no change occurred the prior declaration is validated, otherwise a new DBE is filed. Register of securities movements must mirror every transfer of the fiscal year and be available for audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (Register of Securities Movements - share transfers and members)
Registre des décisions de l'associé unique et procès-verbaux (shareholder decisions and minutes book)
Registre des dirigeants (president and directors register)
Minute book and attendance sheets of shareholder meetings
Registre du commissaire aux comptes (statutory audit file) when an auditor is appointed

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - 1,900 per year (typical French registered-office domiciliation or corporate agent: EUR 200 - 1,700, ex-VAT)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,300 - 17,500 (typical SAS certified audit: EUR 3,000 - 16,000; group/consolidated engagements higher)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for SMEs (turnover < €10 million and taxable profit < €42,500); R&D tax credit (up to 30% of qualifying expenses); innovation status benefits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 - Déclaration de résultat (corporate tax return) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (approximately 3 months)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents declare French-sourced income only; appoint fiscal representative if no permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for expenses, including transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limit deductions to French-source expenses; apply arm's length pricing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: €750 per month of delay (capped); plus 0.75% monthly interest on unpaid tax; possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% on dividends to non-residents (reduced to 0-15% via double tax treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain reduced withholding tax certificate (certificat de résidence) via impots.gouv.fr; submit TRC and beneficial ownership declaration
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% by treaties; Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% by treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group turnover for local file and master file requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to relevant activities (e.g., IP holding, financing); requires adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to €500,000 or 5 years imprisonment for individuals; civil penalties and restitution for companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, possible imprisonment, disqualification from office, and civil liability for damages

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS without sufficient substance for claimed tax benefits or operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of deductions, back taxes, penalties up to 80% of tax due, and potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax debts, possible jail time for fraudulent conduct, and reputational damage

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting or KYC requirements in cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or more; criminal prosecution
